recommendation: ADOPT a symmetric content-based convention: a frozen cross-lineage 'current' citation is read at the citing join's recording heading, and version movement alone does not require a successor. Require a successor when the citer's own lineage moves, when an occupancy consumed as its specification moves, or when any cross-lineage semantic assertion actually relied on by the citer changes. Do not advance PROPOSAL.cross-citation-convention.md unchanged: remeasure and rewrite it against the post-D-292 record, use an unoccupied identifier chosen at dispatch, and define the compared semantic projection explicitly.
rationale: The bytes do show an asymmetric convention: D-269, D-276, D-278, and D-281 refreshed GATE joins after cited ROW successors while preserving reverse ROW citers, and D-288 through D-292 repeated the GATE refresh with unchanged occupancies. The cited predecessor/successor files preserve the same leftoverDesign obligation maps, so those refreshes changed citation currency without changing the allocation relied on. A recording-time reading is the cleaner immutable-artifact rule and avoids version-only cascades. Claude's attached draft nevertheless describes the pre-D-288 snapshot: its proposed identifier is now occupied, its HEAD and COORD pins stop at D-287, and five files it calls current were superseded by D-288 through D-292. It also understates ROW-to-ROW precedent and leaves 'partition the citing join relies on' insufficiently operational. Adoption should therefore be of the convention after a fresh measurement and a precise, symmetric comparison rule, not adoption of the attached bytes as written.

refutations.claim: D-269, D-276, D-278, and D-281 are version-currency precedents in which a GATE join was superseded after a cited ROW join moved while the GATE occupancy stayed unchanged.
refutations.evidence: COORD D-269 keeps G20 occupancy v2 while refreshing sdk v5 to v6; D-276 keeps G18 occupancy v4 after lifecycle v4; D-278 keeps G16 occupancy v5 after monorepo v4; D-281 keeps G08 occupancy v3 after signed-index v4. Each entry records a new GATE leftover-join and says the occupancy is not rewritten.

refutations.claim: The same precedents tolerate the reverse direction by keeping ROW joins current when the GATE join they name is superseded.
refutations.evidence: In the superseding acts themselves, D-276 says lifecycle leftover-join.v4 remains current, D-278 says monorepo leftover-join.v4 remains current, and D-281 says signed-index leftover-join.v4 remains current. Their bytes name g18 v5, g16 v4, and g08 v4 respectively, which those acts supersede.

refutations.claim: ROW-to-ROW citations have no precedent either way.
refutations.evidence: D-282 explicitly keeps packaging leftover-join.v4 current while superseding component-manifest v6 with v9; packaging v4 names component-manifest v6 as current. D-285 explicitly keeps permission leftover-join.v12 current while superseding doctor-actor v11 with v12; permission v12 names doctor-actor v11 as current. These are recorded ROW-to-ROW tolerance precedents.

refutations.claim: D-282 through D-287 were six ROW successors.
refutations.evidence: D-286 records exact-bytes leftover-join.v7 on registerRow DR-G07, and file 08 defines DR-G07 in the gate table. D-282 through D-285 and D-287 are ROW remasurements; D-286 is a GATE remasurement.

refutations.claim: D-288 through D-292 are five GATE citation-refresh successors with unchanged occupancies and no file-08 edit.
refutations.evidence: COORD D-288 records g09 v12, D-289 g12 v5, D-290 g15 v6, D-291 g19 v5, and D-292 g21 v13. Each Decision retains its prior current occupancy, says the cited ROW successor is current, says the old ROW version is not current, and says file 08 is not edited.

refutations.claim: The precedent costs a measured four hours and will recur after every future ROW remasurement.
refutations.evidence: The files contain workflow estimates, not elapsed-time telemetry establishing four hours. The universal recurrence is also false: only a ROW lineage named by a current GATE citation can trigger that directional rule. D-286 is not a ROW lineage, and D-287's distribution-core ROW successor did not itself require any of D-288 through D-292.

refutations.claim: At the proposal's pinned pre-D-288 snapshot, its ten listed citing files, eleven cited-version pairs, hashes, site counts, and byte-identical leftoverDesign partitions are accurate.
refutations.evidence: The ten shasums reproduce the proposal table. Direct comparison reproduces equal summary.leftoverDesign and equal obligations id/leftoverDesign maps for permission v9/v12, doctor-actor v11/v12, component-manifest v6/v9, state-class v3/v4, g18 v5/v6, g16 v4/v5, and g08 v4/v5; the eleven pairs reuse those seven predecessor/successor comparisons. The proposal explicitly pins HEAD 8e3db612e6561b1fa0fab34135b4f6a4252778c4 and last heading D-287.

refutations.claim: Those eleven proposal-table pairs are the current cross-citations at live post-D-292 HEAD.
refutations.evidence: D-288 through D-292 explicitly supersede g09 v11, g12 v4, g15 v5, g19 v4, and g21 v12, five of the proposal's ten citing files. The current stale-citation files are component-manifest v9, doctor-actor v12, lifecycle v4, monorepo v4, packaging v4, permission v12, signed-index v4, and state-class v4; their cited pairs differ from the proposal's pre-D-288 table.

refutations.claim: Seven current ROW joins name a superseded GATE join and are nevertheless kept current.
refutations.evidence: The current bytes are component-manifest v9 to g15 v5, doctor-actor v12 to g12 v4 and g21 v12, permission v12 to g09 v11, state-class v4 to g19 v4, lifecycle v4 to g18 v5, monorepo v4 to g16 v4, and signed-index v4 to g08 v4. COORD D-276, D-278, D-281, D-282, D-283, D-284, and D-285 record those ROW files as current before the cited GATE successors; D-288 through D-292 do not supersede the ROW files.

refutations.claim: The directional rule exists by accident of which side was remasured first.
refutations.evidence: The bytes prove the direction and its repeated application, but no cited COORD entry characterizes its origin as accidental. 'By accident' is an inference, not a recorded fact.

refutations.claim: Equality of the summary leftoverDesign lists alone proves that every semantic fact a citer relies on is unchanged.
refutations.evidence: The current citations assert more than list identity: they name row identity, specific obligation states, ownership/non-stealing relationships, and currentness. The checked predecessor/successor pairs do have equal full obligation id/leftoverDesign maps, which supports this instance, but the proposal does not define which additional cited assertions must be compared for future successors.

refutations.claim: The convention can be recorded without amending D-000 or D-056 and without editing an artifact or file 08.
refutations.evidence: D-000 governs adversarial decision procedure and D-056 governs SATISFIED evidence; neither states a cross-lineage citation-currency rule. The proposal scopes the change to an append-only COORD reading convention and expressly excludes artifact and file-08 edits.

refutations.claim: The attached proposal can be run as the next entry without substantive remeasurement or rewrite.
refutations.evidence: PROPOSAL.cross-citation-convention.md is titled D-288, pins HEAD 8e3db612e6561b1fa0fab34135b4f6a4252778c4, pins the pre-D-288 COORD hash, says the last heading is D-287, and calls five now-superseded GATE joins current. Actual HEAD is 4abb961aad98525ca8b992a24609a6286964a451, actual D-288 is the g09 v12 recording, and D-292 is the last heading. The draft's standing, tables, scope recitals, reversibility text, and identifier are stale.

refutations.claim: Keeping precedent means the next ROW successor necessarily triggers GATE remasurements.
refutations.evidence: A trigger exists only when a current GATE join names that particular ROW version as current. D-287 provides a same-queue counterexample: distribution-core moved, but none of D-288 through D-292 refreshes a citation to distribution-core.

amendments: Remeasure the proposal against the actual post-D-292 HEAD and COORD bytes; replace the occupied draft identifier, stale hashes, last-heading statement, current-file tables, standing text, and reversibility text before review. Choose the next available identifier only when dispatching.
State one symmetric rule for GATE-to-ROW, ROW-to-GATE, and ROW-to-ROW citations: present-tense currentness in a frozen join is evaluated at that join's recording heading.

Define the semantic projection mechanically. For every cross-lineage assertion the citer relies on, compare the referenced obligation's presence and leftoverDesign value and any cited ownership, routing, or status fact; do not use version equality or summary.leftoverDesign alone as the test.
Retain occupancy-consumed-as-specification supersession and own-lineage supersession as independent successor triggers, with no unstated status-token exception.
